Control characters \x0b \x0c \x1b \x7f (and other C0/C1 specials) -> yaml.reader.ReaderError "unacceptable character #x00XX: special characters are not allowed\n  in \"<unicode string>\", position N" (0-based char position).

Exit codes: 0 on success; 1 for any YAML exception (stdout is completely empty, full Python traceback on stderr ending with the line "[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test16' due to unhandled exception!" where <pid> varies per run); 2 for argparse failures ("usage: test16_executable [-h] --a A" then "test16_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --a" or "... error: argument --a: expected one argument").
Argparse caveat for probing/testing: a value starting with '-' (e.g. '-.inf', '---', '---\nfoo') is rejected with exit code 2 unless passed as a single token '--a=<value>'.

Trailing whitespace/newlines in the INPUT are irrelevant to the output: "foo", "foo
", "foo

", "foo   ", "
foo" all produce "foo
...

".
surprises:
The end marker '...' is emitted for a root plain scalar but never for a root collection, quoted string, or block scalar. It is a property of the OUTPUT STYLE of the root node, not of the value's type and not of whether the input had markers. So 'hello' -> "hello
...

" but "hello world: x" (needs quotes) -> "'hello world: x'

" with no marker.

A root string whose dumped form is quoted loses the marker, which means visually similar inputs differ: '42' -> "42
...

" while !!str 42 -> "'42'

".
The empty string dumps to "''\n\n" with NO marker and NO '---', even though an "empty document" in PyYAML's emitter would theoretically force a '---'; that branch is unreachable under SafeDumper.

Non-ASCII content silently changes document framing: 'cafe' -> "cafe
...

" but 'café' -> ""caf\xE9"

" (double-quoted, escaped, no marker) because allow_unicode defaults to false.
Bare '---' is a valid document meaning null (exit 0), but bare '...' is a ParserError (exit 1). Asymmetric.
Whether a leading '---'/'...' forces quoting is a plain 3-character startswith test, so '----' and '...x' are quoted while '--' and 'x...' stay plain - and that flips whether the '...' line appears.

U+0085 (NEL) IS a line break to the parser (so 'ab' becomes the two-line scalar folded to 'a b', still plain, marker present), but U+2028/U+2029 are NOT, and instead force double-quoted output with \L / \P escapes and no marker.
A lone BOM, a lone CR, or a lone NEL as the entire input all parse to null rather than erroring.
!!binary at the root produces a block literal ('!!binary |') whose body already ends at column 0, so dump adds no extra blank line and no '...' - total stdout is body + one '\n' from print.
A root collection that is self-referential emits a bare anchor line ('&id001') as the first line of output - the closest the output ever gets to having a document-header line, and still no '---'.
Multiple documents are an error rather than dumping only the first, and when the first document is empty the ComposerError message drops its first location block entirely, changing the message shape.

yaml.dump's output always ends in exactly one newline, and the script's print() adds a second, so every successful stdout ends with a blank line; implementations that emit only one trailing newline will mismatch on every single case.
